ops.grounding: 625-segmentation-substrate g4-integrate: a self-authored full-physics-suite regression check (py -m pytest tests/unit/physics -q, folded into a Commander closing postcondition) ran as a harness-tracked background task and was killed/reaped by the harness at ~90% complete after ~60-90 min wall clock, exactly matching this lesson's core claim ('A commander's harness-tracked background workers die... guaranteed strand'). No Admiral-owned OS-detached watcher was available in this one-issue delegated dispatch. Recovered by floating to the reachable Admiral (team-lead), who authorized a scoped fallback (grep the real import graph of changed files, run only those tests -- 170/170 pass -- plus reuse the partial 90%-clean run as corroborating evidence), then waived the original postcondition through the engine with that authority cited. Extends the lesson: when Admiral-owned detached infra isn't available, a Commander should size a self-authored full-suite check's runtime BEFORE freezing it into a gate plan (or scope it to the actual import-graph risk surface from the start) rather than discovering the cost only when it blocks closeout.

625-segmentation-substrate: every one of 4 gates' IMPLEMENTER_RESULT/REVIEW_RESULT claims was independently re-run and reproduced by the commander before integrating (test counts, real-data script outputs incl. the F12 real-data verdict reproduced byte-identical on a fresh 5m49s run, git diff/status scope checks, evo-import greps) -- caught nothing false this run, but the discipline held throughout and is what let the F12 FAIL verdict be trusted as genuine rather than taken on a crew's word.

625-segmentation-substrate: all 8 crew dispatches (g1-g4 implement+review) used the Agent tool with run_crew.py --dispatch external registering each attempt in crew-runs.json, --verify-result confirming freshness, recover_crews.py run before each dispatch -- no claude CLI binary in this harness, standing misfit navigated consistently.

625-segmentation-substrate: attach (not attest) used for every artifact-checked postcondition (user-decision at understand/plan/triage/review; implementer-result/review-result at every gN-implement/gN-review); attest --which preconditions/postconditions used only for check:null conditions; attest correctly refused on command-checked conditions (advance run instead).

ops.statement: When a Commander's OWN plan (not a launch-order-mandated check) folds a full-repo/full-suite regression command into a gate's closing postcondition, grep the actual import graph of the changed files FIRST and consider scoping the check to real importers -- a blanket 'run everything' check on a numerics-heavy suite can take 60-90+ minutes and get reaped by the harness before completion, forcing an emergency float-and-waive at the worst possible time (finalization). A targeted subset covering every actual importer is both faster and arguably more correctly scoped to the real risk surface.
ops.grounding: 625-segmentation-substrate g4-integrate: py -m pytest tests/unit/physics -q (self-authored, ~15k+ tests) was reaped twice (~90% and again mid-run) before completing; a grep for real importers of the two changed existing files (arcs.py, segment_classifier.py) found only 7 test files (170 tests total), which ran clean in ~21 minutes and, combined with the reaped run's 90%-clean partial coverage, gave equally strong regression evidence at a fraction of the cost -- discovered only AFTER the expensive check was already blocking closeout, not planned in from the start.
ops.bank_reason: Only one occurrence so far (this run) -- needs re-observation across a couple more Commander runs that fold a self-authored full-suite check into a gate to confirm this is a recurring planning gap (not a one-off) before it graduates to a stronger doctrine statement (e.g. a standing rule in commander-core.md's gate-planning section about sizing verification cost before freezing it into a plan).
